performers: Orquestra de música antiga de l’Esmuc; Alba Roca, concertmaster and director
intro: The Chaconne from Act V of Purcell’s The Fairy Queen, Z. 629, is a dance in triple time in which the bass stops for sixteen bars. Alba Roca directs the ESMUC early-music orchestra.

sections.label: A · Dotted strings over a walking bass
sections.mNote: Dotted violin phrases above three steady bass notes

sections.label: B · Violins in quicker running notes
sections.mNote: The violins play quicker notes in the same three-beat dance.

sections.label: C · Violins and viola without bass
sections.mNote: Violins and viola trade short phrases.

sections.label: D · Bass returns
sections.mNote: Short bass notes alternate with rests

sections.label: E · Moving bass beneath the violins
sections.mNote: Moving bass notes under the final dance phrases

cues.title: Chaconne, bars 1–16, bass
cues.text: The bass moves in three even steps in each bar. Above it, the violins and viola play dotted rhythms, a long note followed by a short one.
cues.evidence: Purcell, Suite from The Fairy Queen, edited by J. S. Shedlock, typeset by Bart Dunn, Chaconne, bars 1–16, printed p. 48. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/6/69/IMSLP435506-PMLP237007-Suite_from_The_Fairy_Queen_Complete.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Concert recording, Barcelona, 2018
cues.text: The performance took place in the Sala de teclats, the keyboard room of Barcelona’s Museu de la Música, on 7 April 2018. Alba Roca directed the ESMUC early-music orchestra, and the student sound engineer Marc Urrutia recorded the concert.
cues.evidence: The ESMUC recording credits name the Sala de teclats, Museu de la Música de Barcelona, Alba Roca, Marc Urrutia and the concert date. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Purcell_TheFairyQueen_ActV_Chaconne_Z629_Esmuc.flac

cues.title: Bars 49–64, bass rests
cues.text: For sixteen bars the bass rests. The violins and viola pass short phrases between them, and the violins often leave the first beat empty. The triple metre continues.
cues.evidence: Shedlock–Dunn score, Chaconne, bars 49–64, printed pp. 50–51: the basso rests throughout; violin rests and viola entries alternate.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: First production, Dorset Garden, 1692
cues.text: In May 1692 the Queen’s Theatre at Dorset Garden staged The Fairy Queen, a spoken adaptation of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream with a masque in each later act. Lost after Purcell’s death, the score reappeared in the Royal Academy of Music library before the Purcell Society printed it in 1903.
cues.evidence: Preface to The Works of Henry Purcell, vol. XII (Purcell Society, ed. J. S. Shedlock, Novello, 1903), pp. i–iv: an anonymous adaptation of A Midsummer Night’s Dream produced at the Queen’s (formerly the Dorset Garden) Theatre and reported in the Gentleman’s Journal for May 1692; the long-lost score found in the library of the Royal Academy of Music; the extra Act I music dates from the 1693 revival. The edition’s contents show the masques of songs and dances in Acts II–V and the Chaconne ending Act V: https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/f/f5/IMSLP611116-PMLP237007-92329-00.fsc.pdf . Andrew Pinnock’s note to Signum SIGCD615 on the production: https://www.hyperion-records.co.uk/dc.asp?dc=D_SIGCD615

cues.title: Running bass, from bar 82
cues.text: From bar 82 the bass moves in quicker notes beneath the violins. The first violin adds short flourishes above it, and all four parts are again fully occupied.
cues.evidence: Shedlock–Dunn score, Chaconne, printed pp. 51–53, especially the running basso from bar 82.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

transitions.title: The violins quicken
transitions.from: A · Dotted strings over a walking bass
transitions.to: B · Violins in quicker running notes
transitions.how: The two violins take up quicker dotted figures in bars 16–22. The basso keeps its three crotchets to the bar, and the viola punctuates the new violin writing with notes and rests. The dance stays in 3/4.
transitions.evidence: Shedlock–Dunn score, Chaconne, bars 16–22, printed p. 48: quicker violin figures above the continuing bass crotchets.

transitions.title: The basso drops out
transitions.from: B · Violins in quicker running notes
transitions.to: C · Violins and viola without bass
transitions.how: After the four parts reach the end of the phrase together, the basso rests for sixteen bars, from bar 49 in the Shedlock–Dunn score. The three upper strings play on without it. The viola starts the next figure, and the violins rest on the first beat before they enter.
transitions.evidence: Shedlock–Dunn score, Chaconne, bars 48–64, printed pp. 50–51: the basso stops at bar 49; the three upper parts continue.

transitions.title: The bass returns between rests
transitions.from: C · Violins and viola without bass
transitions.how: The basso returns with three repeated crotchets. Bass and viola then alternate short notes with rests beneath the violins’ dotted phrases.
transitions.evidence: Shedlock–Dunn score, Chaconne, bars 65–77, printed p. 51: repeated bass notes at bar 65, followed by notes separated by rests.

transitions.title: Running figures pass to the bass
transitions.to: E · Moving bass beneath the violins
transitions.how: From bar 78 the first violin adds quick flourishes to its dotted phrases. At bar 82 the basso moves from longer notes into running figures, which fill the places taken earlier by rests. The running bass continues towards the close of the Chaconne.
transitions.evidence: Shedlock–Dunn score, Chaconne, bars 78–84 and following, printed pp. 51–53: violin flourishes and the running basso from bar 82.

source.title: Purcell, The Fairy Queen — instrumental suite, Bart Dunn typesetting after Shedlock
source.locator: Chaconne, printed pp. 48–53: two violin parts, viola and basso. The cello desk represents the written basso part.

timeline.note: The violins and viola play dotted phrases above three steady bass notes in each bar.
The basso rests for bars 49–64; the violins and viola pass short phrases between them.
The basso returns with repeated notes, then leaves rests between its phrases.
Running bass notes support the violins’ dotted phrases and short flourishes.

fields.label: Work version
fields.value: Original four-part instrumental dance; sounding pitch approximately A=415
fields.note: The file identifies the Act V Chaconne. Approximate pitch is inferred by comparing its written C-major ending with the recording’s prominent sustained peaks near 494–495 Hz, about a semitone below modern C5. The session source does not state a tuning reference; no exact temperament or edition is claimed.
